migration_apply_step_verdict.reasoning: job.services.<service_id>.id is documented GHA job-context syntax for a service container's Docker network ID, usable in docker exec from a step running directly on the runner (this job does not declare `container:`, so it runs on the VM itself and can freely docker exec into any sibling container including services). Verified the glob+order replication is exact: both migrate.go's fs.Glob("*.up.sql")+sort.Strings and the CI shell's `for file in server/migrations/*.up.sql` pick up the same 5 files in the same order and both structurally exclude 0001_init.sql (wrong glob suffix), which is independently confirmed dead/Postgres-only by content inspection. Re-running the exact step logic end-to-end against a live mariadb:11.4 container produced a correct schema and the exact admin-count=2 the AC requires.
migration_apply_step_verdict.docker_exec_vs_direct_mysql_client: The implementer's stated reasoning (mariadb/mysql CLI presence on ubuntu-latest not guaranteed, service image always has one) is a defensible, cautious choice and the step works correctly as verified. It is, however, not the most idiomatic pattern: GitHub's own documented pattern for MySQL/MariaDB service containers used from a job running directly on the runner (not inside a `container:`) is to connect directly via the already-mapped port (`ports: - 3306:3306` already present in this file) using a `mysql` client, since GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner images document a MySQL client as pre-installed software — making the 'CLI not guaranteed' premise somewhat overstated, though not wrong to hedge against. Net: sound and verified-working, but a future simplification pass could drop the docker-exec indirection in favor of `mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306` directly from the runner. Not blocking.

findings.title: Migration-apply step uses docker exec into the service container rather than the more idiomatic mapped-port connection
findings.description: test.yml's 'Apply migrations' step (lines 68-75) uses `docker exec -i "${{ job.services.mariadb.id }}" mariadb ...` to feed each migration file into the service container. Since the mariadb service already publishes `ports: - 3306:3306` to the runner and this job does not run inside a `container:` (so localhost networking to services works directly), GitHub's own documented pattern for this scenario is to connect straight to 127.0.0.1:3306 with a mysql client already available on ubuntu-latest runner images. The implementer's stated concern (mariadb/mysql CLI not guaranteed present) is a reasonable hedge but somewhat overstated given GH's runner-images software list documents a MySQL client as pre-installed.
findings.impact: None currently — independently re-ran this exact step against a live mariadb:11.4 container and it produced the correct schema and admin count. Purely a style/robustness preference, not a functional defect.
findings.recommendation: Optional future simplification: replace the docker exec loop with `mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -uroot -p"$MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD" "$MARIADB_DATABASE" < "$file"` (installing mysql-client via apt first if not already present, matching GitHub's own MySQL service-container doc example). Not required — current implementation is correct and verified working.

findings.title: Migration-apply step does not populate schema_migrations bookkeeping table
findings.description: migrate.go's Run() creates schema_migrations (ensureSchemaMigrations) and records one row per applied version. test.yml's 'Apply migrations' step feeds the raw *.up.sql files directly via mariadb client and never touches schema_migrations, so the CI-built schema is not byte-for-byte identical to what the app's own startup migration runner would produce.
findings.impact: None today — confirmed via grep that no test file (access_repo_test.go, store_test.go, auth_test.go) references schema_migrations, and a fresh single-run CI database has no need for the applied/skip bookkeeping migrate.go uses for idempotent re-runs. Would only matter if a future test started asserting against schema_migrations contents.
findings.recommendation: No action required. If ever relevant, the step could additionally CREATE TABLE schema_migrations and INSERT one row per applied version to fully mirror migrate.go, but this is not needed for current test coverage.

findings.title: `.env` heredoc's CONTACT_EMAIL=${CONTACT_EMAIL:-} deviation is not strictly load-bearing against the failure mode it targets
findings.description: The implementer added `:-` fallback specifically to CONTACT_EMAIL (deploy.yml:251) to avoid `set -euo pipefail` aborting on an unbound variable if the GitHub secret doesn't exist yet. Under GitHub Actions semantics, however, a reference to a nonexistent secret (`${{ secrets.CONTACT_EMAIL }}`) evaluates to an empty string at expression-resolution time, not an omitted key — so the env: block (deploy.yml:109) and the envs: allowlist always define CONTACT_EMAIL as an exported, defined-but-possibly-empty variable in the remote script's environment. Bash's `set -u` does not treat 'defined but empty' as unbound, so the plain `${CONTACT_EMAIL}` form (used by every other var in the same heredoc) would not actually have aborted the script in the scenario described. The parallel security-auditor pass reached the identical conclusion independently (targeted_check_results #4 in security-auditor-1.json).
findings.impact: None — the fallback is redundant defense, not incorrect. Does not mask a required credential's absence (no other var shares this treatment) and does not affect correctness of any of the 5 CONTACT_EMAIL hops.
findings.recommendation: No action required; harmless. If precision matters, the deviation note in decisions.md could be phrased as 'defensive belt-and-suspenders' rather than implying it prevents an abort that would not have actually occurred.

findings.title: No concurrency group on test.yml's push/pull_request triggers
findings.description: test.yml triggers on both `push: branches: ["**"]` and `pull_request:` with no `concurrency:` block. A PR opened from a branch in the same repository (not a fork) will trigger two independent, simultaneous runs of the same test suite — one for the push event, one for the pull_request event.
findings.impact: Doubles CI minutes consumed per same-repo PR push; not a correctness issue since both runs are legitimate and both must pass for the intended feedback loop to work.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a `concurrency: group: test-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }} cancel-in-progress: true` block to dedupe. Not required by the task spec and not blocking.
